title: Man shot dead by officer had fired on police before ; Biker killed by OPP held Montreal officer hostage in early '90s: [Ontario Edition]
article: A Quebec man killed after an Ontario Provincial Police officer was shot in a gunfight on Highway 401 had been involved in a previous police shooting.
Daniel Lamer, an associate of the Nomads, the most vicious segment of the Hells Angels motorcycle gang, shot OPP Constable Dan Brisson at close range Sunday, a police source said.
Brisson's body armour was credited for saving his life. The OPP officers on the scene then shot and killed Lamer.
A police source said Lamer spent 14 of his 37 years in maximum- security prisons, mostly in Quebec, and was a wanted escaper when he died.
In the early 1990s, Lamer took a Montreal police officer hostage and shot him when he tried to escape, the source said.

Lamer had escaped from a maximum-security prison and joined another man in a drugstore robbery that netted less than $100. He and his partner were cornered by police in a nearby bar but managed to disarm one of the officers and take him hostage.
After restraining the officer with his own handcuffs, the two men put a gun to his head and, using the officer as a shield, escaped in a stolen car.
When they ran into a roadblock, the duo fled with the handcuffed officer to a house and took the occupant hostage.

After a 16-hour standoff, the officer slipped out of his handcuffs and grabbed his service weapon when his captors fell asleep. But before he was able to flee, he was shot twice in the leg. He still managed to jump from a window and escape.
In a bizarre turn of events, Lamer and his cohort released the second hostage, but shot each other in an argument about whether they should surrender.
Lamer went back to prison, and was paroled in 1999.

His parole was revoked early last year and a warrant was issued for his arrest after he escaped from police in Laval. He bolted over rooftops after they searched his vehicle and found a gun, balaclava and gloves.

Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, which probes all cases involving police officers where death or serious injury results, would not comment on Lamer's criminal history. OPP spokesperson Sergeant Kristine Cholette didn't comment either, saying the matter was under SIU control.

Brisson, 28, the officer shot on Sunday just west of the Upper Canada Rd. exit on Highway 401 in Brockville, was injured in the shooting as a bullet ricocheted off his body armour, hitting the officer along the back of the neck and head.
Lamer, 37, also wore body armour, but he was shot in the head.
Sources told The Star Brisson had pulled over a red Pontiac Sunfire with Quebec plates for speeding. As he approached the car, he noticed the two occupants were wearing bulletproof vests.
The officer pulled back and called for backup. When two other officers arrived, including an officer who spoke French, the driver was ordered from the car and came quietly.
However, Lamer emerged firing and was shot dead, the source said.
SIU investigators have now designated two OPP officers as witnesses, as opposed to subject officers- those whose conduct appears to have caused a death or serious injury.
Brisson joined the OPP last November after serving less than two years on the Toronto police force. A Toronto spokesperson said he joined the force in February, 2000.
Cholette said the officer is out of hospital and doing well.

The OPP has charged the other occupant of the car, 27-year-old Marc Bouffard of St-Lin, Laurentide, Que., with obstructing justice by attempting to escape, impersonation and public mischief for presenting himself as another person.
Bouffard, who is represented by Montreal lawyer Gilbert Frigond, is to appear in a Cornwall court on April 2.
Police sources said Bouffard is a member of the Montreal Rockers, a club affiliated with the Hells Angels biker gang.
